question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic code execution from connected Android nodes, and should the high-power pieces use the generic node-hosted tool contract tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8287 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90431?
rationale: The remaining work changes phone authority, private-data access, and model-visible execution boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/security shape safely.

options.title: Split safe Android controls first
options.body: Implement only narrow brightness, volume, vibration, or similar Android controls after explicit permission UX and node command-policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

options.title: Route through generic node tools
options.body: Use the node-hosted tool design path as the core contract and let Android expose approved descriptors only after that contract lands with provenance and allow/deny semantics.

options.title: Keep high-power execution out of core
options.body: Reject ADB and dynamic Android code execution in OpenClaw core for now and require external plugins, ClawHub packages, or app-specific forks for that authority.

recommendation.title: Split safe Android controls first
recommendation.body: Implement only narrow brightness, volume, vibration, or similar Android controls after explicit permission UX and node command-policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the open node-hosted tools candidate and is the clearest current routing signal for the node-to-model security boundary.
